title: In 2017–18, 2,500 volunteers counted tiny pores on ginkgo leaves to study the ancient atmosphere; 24,000 classifications helped process the images
description: Ginkgo trees, which have existed for millions of years, provide valuable information on historical carbon dioxide levels. Researchers employ citizen volunteers to count leaf pores, enhancing the study's efficiency. Initial test phases revealed varying accuracy levels among volunteers but still yielded useful data. Methods to correct classifications have improved the reliability of the results significantly. This collaborative effort fosters public engagement with climate science and enhances research productivity.

title: Nadirah’s 3D-printed ceramics explore the tension between ancient clay and digital precision

title: Exploring Iran's Ancient Civilization: New Digital Resources Highlight Persia's Enduring Cultural Legacy
description: A new digital exploration of Iranian history and civilization offers audiences worldwide an opportunity to discover the rich legacy of ancient Persia, from the Achaemenid Empire and the monumental cities of Persepolis and Susa to the Parthian and Sasanian periods.
